title: Why Your Students Need To Hear The Hard Truth
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Prompted by a news story about a fatal group assault by students with a long history of unpunished bullying, Linsin argues that dishonesty -- however well-intentioned -- is what allows minor misbehavior to calcify into serious harm. His central claim is that shielding students from truthful, direct feedback about their conduct, in favor of counseling, restorative circles, or excuse-making tied to home life or learning differences, does not protect them but instead plants the seeds of unaccountable, remorseless behavior. He is careful to say he isn't blaming individual teachers, but he presses the uncomfortable question of whether consistent, honest accountability over years might have changed the trajectory of students who ultimately killed a classmate. The piece functions as a moral argument for the SCM principle that consequences and honest feedback, not appeasement, are what actually protect students and their communities.
points: Dishonesty about student behavior, no matter how gently intentioned, guarantees students never get the feedback needed to improve or to internalize right and wrong.
Repeated appeasement, false praise, and excuse-making for chronic misbehavior can grow into narcissism and a sense of consequence-free entitlement over years.
Counseling, restorative circles, and social-emotional programming without genuine accountability plant a seed rather than solve the underlying problem.
Honest, consistently enforced accountability early on is framed as a form of protection for both the misbehaving student and their community.
